task.name: Two re-entry paths resume a stopped story differently, and which one is chosen decides whether review runs
task.story_text:
## Why

Two commands re-enter a story that stopped mid-pipeline, they do materially different things, and
nothing tells an operator which one to use.

`forge review` runs the review phase against a worktree. `forge sprint --resume` re-enters the
pipeline, recovers the phase records an earlier attempt produced, and continues from where the
recovered state leaves it. From the same stopped story, those produce different outcomes.

Observed directly: a story stopped after its review requested changes, the fix was made, the gate
passed, and the second review cycle was refused for lack of funds. Two re-entry paths were
available. `forge review` would have run the missing review cycle. `forge sprint --resume`
recovered the escalation decision recorded against the story and proceeded to the landing step
instead — so the review cycle that had never run was not run, and the recorded decision stood in
its place.

Both behaviours are defensible. Neither is discoverable. An operator choosing between them is
choosing whether the work gets reviewed, and nothing at the point of choice says so.

The general-purpose command being the one that skips review is the part most likely to surprise:
`--resume` reads as "continue what you were doing", and continuing is what it did — it just
continued from a decision rather than from the unfinished phase.

## Acceptance criteria

- An operator inspecting a stopped story can see which phases it still has outstanding and what
  re-entering will do, before spending anything.
- Re-entry reports which recovered state it is acting on when that state changes the path taken —
  in particular when a recorded decision causes a phase to be skipped rather than run.
- A story that has an unrun review cycle is distinguishable from one whose review completed, in
  both the status surface and whatever re-entry reports before it starts.
- Where more than one re-entry path applies, the documentation states which to use for which
  stopped state, so the choice is not made by guessing.

## Example

The same stopped story, two re-entry paths, different outcomes:

```
state:  gate PASS · review cycle 1 REQUEST_CHANGES · fix committed · cycle 2 never ran
        escalation decision recorded: land_core_defer_edges

forge review <worktree>        -> runs review cycle 2 against the fix
forge sprint --resume          -> recovers the decision, proceeds to landing; no review runs
```

Nothing in the status output, the pending-decision display, or either command's help distinguishes
these, and the second is the one an operator reaches for by default.

handoff.summary: Added a single deterministic re-entry analysis over the existing resume sidecar and surfaced it on every surface an operator consults before spending. resume_persistence.py gains a `review_progress` sibling key (reviewer cycles, latest verdict, gate decision/commit, counters) written alongside existing phase blocks, plus classify_review_obligation()/analyze_reentry()/describe_reentry_paths()/load_reentry_analysis() as the one derivation of 'the next review cycle has not run' vs 'review completed' vs 'unknown'. The key is deliberately not a PHASE_BLOCKS member: it is never reported in recovered_phases/recorded_phases, never decides record usability, and never alone causes a record to be written, so existing recovery reporting and validation are unchanged. recover_phase_state() now returns a reentry_impact block when a genuinely recovered escalate-gate decision coincides with an outstanding review cycle; run_setup._report_reentry_impact() prints three short ↺ RESUME lines naming the decision, source run, outstanding cycle (with last verdict and gate decision) and the fact that this resume will NOT run REVIEW while `forge review` would. StoryStatusEntry gains outstanding_phases/reentry_note, populated by read_live_status() and read_completed_status() (which took an optional project_root, passed by its single caller) and rendered as `outstanding:` / `re-entry:` lines under each story row; _show_pending_decisions() prints the same two lines. cli-reference.md gains a 'Choosing a re-entry path' section with the stopped-state table, cross-linked from --resume, forge review, forge status and the Resume behavior table.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1: the re-entry disclosure was wired into _setup_resume_entry, which forge review and the pipeline resume both go through, so forge review printed the resume's 'will NOT run REVIEW' wording immediately before running REVIEW. Added REENTRY_MODE_REVIEW / REENTRY_MODE_PIPELINE_RESUME constants in run_setup.py and threaded an explicit reentry_mode keyword from cmd_review through run_from_review and _run_resume_coordinator into _setup_resume_entry, which passes it to _report_reentry_impact. The shared first two lines (recovered escalation decision + source run; outstanding REVIEW cycle with last verdict and gate decision) are unchanged on both paths; only the final line differs — the review path says it runs the cycle now and that sprint --resume would skip it, the resume path keeps the original wording. The mode is stamped onto the reentry_impact dict before it reaches state.phase_recovery so the audit records which disclosure was made. The default is pipeline_resume deliberately: a --resume triage can dispatch to run_from_review too, so only forge review declares itself. The first disclosure line was reworded from 'acting on escalation decision' to 'recovered escalation decision' since 'acting on' overstated it for the review path; docs updated to match and to show both variants. Iteration 0 (unchanged this cycle) added the review_progress sidecar key, classify_review_obligation/analyze_reentry/describe_reentry_paths/load_reentry_analysis, StoryStatusEntry.outstanding_phases/reentry_note rendered in forge status rows and pending decisions, and the cli-reference 'Choosing a re-entry path' section.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 says StoryStatusEntry re-entry fields are populated by both read_live_status() and read_completed_status(), partly from the resume sidecar — but read_completed_status(summary_path: Path) (src/theforge/sprint/status_reader.py:878) has no project_root, and resume_record_path()/load_resume_record() require one to locate .forge/<...>/resume records.
  Suggestion: Either derive project_root from summary_path, or add an optional project_root kwarg — the only caller is src/theforge/cli/sprint_status.py:208, so the signature change is contained. Alternatively scope sidecar-derived fields to read_live_status() and populate the completed path from the summary/audit data only.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 adds a non-phase key to the resume record. merge_resume_record() merges generically and _METADATA_KEYS/PHASE_BLOCKS are separate lists, so an unregistered key survives a merge, but validate_resume_record()'s usability check at resume_persistence.py:321 keys off PHASE_BLOCKS + complexity_routing_audit, and recovered_phases/recorded_phases are built from PHASE_BLOCKS only.
  Suggestion: Decide explicitly whether the review-progress facts are a new PHASE_BLOCKS entry or a sibling metadata key, and keep it out of recovered_phases so the existing '↺ RESUME recovered phase record: …' line does not start naming a non-phase. RECORD_VERSION need not bump for an additive key since older records simply lack it — but the dev should confirm the absent-key path returns 'no review obligation known' rather than 'review completed'.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's message enumerates source run, recovered phase, decision, selected_action, outstanding cycle and both command behaviours on one RESUME line; the surrounding _cu._log lines in run_setup.py are single short lines.
  Suggestion: Allow the dev to split it across two or three '  ↺ RESUME' lines rather than forcing one long line.

finding_registry.description: When forge review re-enters a story with a recovered escalation decision and an outstanding review cycle, startup output says this resume will not run REVIEW even though forge review proceeds into the review phase.

When a stopped story is shown through the completed-sprint forge status path, the failed story row omits the outstanding REVIEW cycle and the note that forge review and forge sprint --resume take different re-entry paths.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
